description: Trae Agent is an LLM-based agent for general purpose software engineering tasks.

summary.one_liner: Trae Agent is an LLM-based command-line agent that takes natural-language instructions and carries out general software engineering tasks using tools such as bash, file editing, and sequential thinking.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a `trae-cli` command with run, show-config, and interactive modes for executing coding tasks from natural language. The agent uses a toolset that includes bash execution, a string-replace-based file edit tool, sequential thinking, and a task_done tool. It supports multiple LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Doubao, Azure, OpenRouter, Ollama, Google Gemini) configured through a YAML file or environment variables. It can optionally run tasks inside Docker containers, either from an image, a Dockerfile, a tar image file, or an existing container. It records execution trajectories to JSON for debugging and analysis, and supports optional MCP servers such as Playwright.
use_cases: automate multi-step software engineering tasks from plain-English instructions
fix bugs or add tests in a local project directory
run LLM coding agent experiments or ablation studies
run agent tasks inside an isolated Docker container
record and inspect agent action trajectories for debugging
use local models through Ollama for code edits
how_to_run: trae-cli run "Create a hello world Python script"
stack: Node.js npx for Playwright MCP example
notable: Modular, transparent architecture designed for modifying and studying agent designs and ablation studies
Lakeview feature that gives short summaries of agent steps
Docker mode with several options for image, Dockerfile, tar archive, or existing container
Trajectory recording of LLM calls, steps, and tool usage to JSON
Configuration priority: CLI arguments, then config file, then environment variables, then defaults
caveats: Project is described as still under active development
Requires an API key for a chosen LLM provider
Docker mode requires Docker to be installed and configured
README lists UV as a requirement but the install line is incomplete in the source text
